newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - UK's BoE move important in long term.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - UK's BoE move important in long term.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday that the most important element in Britain's decision to increase the independence of the Bank of England was the impact this would have on long-term policy.

"The most important aspect of the British decision is, in my view, the reasoning given -- that is the fact that they have made clear that they are interested in a longer-term stability orientation for monetary policy," he told German ZDF television.
"They are even talking about so-called long-termism. That is important," he added.
The newly-elected Labour government gave the British central bank freedom to set interest rate levels earlier this week, but said the Treasury would continue to set inflation targets.
The decision was widely seen as a pro-European move, even though Britain is not expected to join the single European currency for some years to come.

In the television interview, Tietmeyer repeated his view that Britain had now come some way toward fulfilling the Maastricht Treaty requirement that single currency members must have fully independent central banks.
"The current decision is a step toward the requirements laid down by the Maastricht Treaty," he said.
He added that the independence of central banks, and notably the European Central Bank, would be important for the stability of the single currency.
The success of the central bank in asserting its independence would depend to a great extent on "the personalities involved," he said.

Tietmeyer has given clear public support to the idea that Wim Duisenberg, the Dutch central bank head who will take over as head of the European Monetary Institute from the middle of this year, should also lead the future ECB.
